notice: ASL (American Sign Language) is a distinct language from JSL. Signs vary by region and signer; illustrations are learning aids, not authoritative instruction.

entries.description: Raise an open right hand near the forehead and move it outward in a small salute-like wave. Keep the motion relaxed and use a friendly expression.
Touch the fingertips of a flat hand near the chin, then move the hand forward toward the person. Pair the movement with an appreciative expression.
Place a flat hand on the chest and move it in a small circular motion. Hand orientation and movement should be checked against a fluent signer.
Make a fist and move it in a small circle on the chest. Facial expression helps convey the apology.
A common ASL expression combines GOOD and MORNING. Learn the two signs in sequence from a fluent model; the icon is a reminder, not a handshape diagram.
ASL commonly combines GOOD and NIGHT. Keep the signs distinct and follow the timing and orientation shown by a fluent signer.
Wave an open hand toward the other person. The expression and direction of the wave help make the farewell clear.
A common ASL sign moves a flat hand from the chin outward. This forms part of expressions such as GOOD MORNING and GOOD NIGHT.
Hold up an open hand with all five fingers extended. Pay attention to palm orientation and signing space.
ASL number ten is commonly shown with a thumbs-up handshape and a small twist. Confirm the movement with a fluent ASL model.
Point to yourself to refer to ME or I. Pronoun placement is meaningful; use the signing space consistently.
The common ASL sign NAME uses both index and middle fingers extended, touching together. Proper names can also be fingerspelled.
A natural ASL introduction may use NICE, MEET, and YOU in sequence. Maintain eye contact and appropriate facial grammar.
The common ASL sign LIKE uses the thumb and middle finger near the chest, then moves the hand outward. Facial expression can affect meaning.
Make a fist and nod it up and down like a head nod. Natural facial expression and conversational timing matter.
The ASL sign HELP commonly places one fist on the palm of the other hand and lifts both hands. Practice orientation and movement with a trusted source.
